title: Counted fields

reference.grammar: Tone set as a count of single dots, in a dark green and a teal on white.

techniques.name: Counted screen

cell.label: Cell
cell.note: Side of one screen cell, in screen pixels. Held at this size at any plate size, so a larger plate prints more dots, not bigger ones.

dot.label: Dot
dot.note: Side of one dot, in screen pixels. Dots print as whole pixels; a fractional size is kept by thinning the count, so tone does not jump.

perCell.label: Dots per cell
perCell.note: Most dots one cell can hold. Tone is the count: density times this, the remainder kept by the hash.

jitter.label: Scatter
jitter.note: Where a dot may land in its cell. 1 is anywhere (the stochastic screen); 0 stacks every dot on the cell center, an ordered screen.

round.label: Round from
round.note: Dots this size and larger print round; smaller ones are square pixels.

seed.label: Seed
seed.note: Re-rolls every hash: which dots are kept and where they land.

techniques.implementation: Each cell of a jittered grid prints up to N dots at hashed positions and keeps the last one with probability equal to the remainder, so density is carried by the count of marks and nothing is blended.

techniques.name: Stipple ramps

gamma.label: Ramp curve
gamma.note: First figure: density = floor + (top - floor) · x^curve across the width.

gamma2.label: Split ramp curve
gamma2.note: Second figure: the same ramp, printed dark green over teal.

split.label: Split
split.note: Where the second figure turns from dark green to teal, with a hairline on the seam.

techniques.implementation: density = floor + (top - floor) · (x / W)^curve, screened by the counted screen; the split ramp prints the top in dark green and the bottom in teal.

techniques.name: Ring interference

pitchA.label: Pitch, you
pitchA.note: Ring pitch of the first source, in figure units.

pitchB.label: Pitch, Mir
pitchB.note: Ring pitch of the second source. Close to the first, the beat between them opens into wide lozenges.

gain.label: Gain
gain.note: Density at a shared crest: (0.02 + gain · (A·B)^1.25) under the falloff.

reach.label: Reach
reach.note: Width of the falloff that fades the rings toward the edges, as a share of the figure width.

peak.label: Purple peak
peak.note: Where both crests stand above this near the first source, the cell prints one purple count. 1 removes it.

techniques.implementation: Two ring screens A = ½ + ½cos(2π dA / pA) and B likewise; their product, under a gaussian falloff, is the density; the cell takes dark green where A leads and teal where B does.

techniques.name: Counted letters

tone.label: Tone
tone.note: Each letter prints its digit (1 to 9, from its place in the alphabet) as density digit/9 times this.

inset.label: Inset
inset.note: Margin of white inside each cell, in figure units.

techniques.implementation: The words are spelled one letter per cell; each letter maps to a digit 1 to 9 and the cell prints that count as its tone, in the ink of its channel.

techniques.name: Measured inks
techniques.implementation: solid ink pixels of each figure, read at full resolution, are clustered to five colors; a color is kept when it holds at least 4% of the ink.

techniques.name: Figure and ground
techniques.implementation: The ground is the most common border color of a figure; ink is every pixel more than 40 levels from it.

techniques.name: Justified plate
techniques.implementation: Figures keep their proportions and share a row height; each row fills the plate width. Every split of the figures into rows is tried, and the one whose row heights sit closest to the target wins.

pass_order: counted screen · cells at screen size
ramps · rings · counted letters, one density field each
read · points measured from the filed figures
